topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic changes and the conditions for cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can drive clonal evolution when cellular susceptibility and the surrounding microenvironment permit cancer to develop.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than cancer being solely a matter of inherited susceptibility or bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations, with their effects shaped by metabolic activation and tissue-specific processing.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require a separate growth-promoting environment for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue specificity of carcinogen effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how susceptibility to carcinogens depends on the exposed tissue's state and consolidate the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence is gathered to identify carcinogenic exposures and why establishing their effects remains difficult.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and the difficulty of assessing them to frame everyday risk–benefit decisions.
